title: Adaptive client resume protocols and compatibility checklist for pagination, retries, and streaming
creator: Evelyn Chen
description: PRD describing required client-side semantics and acceptance tests for cross-language SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) to support resumable streams, idempotent pagination, and standardized retry/backoff behavior while preserving backwards compatibility.
background: Multiple customers reported partial failures when downgrading to older clients during a streaming cutover; incidents showed inconsistent cursor encodings and opaque retry states. The SDKs have historically diverged in how they represent stream checkpoints and how cursor expiration is surfaced to the app. This PRD consolidates a migration-safe protocol and a checklist to validate polyglot client behavior.
goals: Define a language-agnostic resume protocol for event/response streams with explicit checkpoints
Standardize cursor format that is backwards-tolerant and encryptable (client-side opaque token)
Specify retry semantics (idempotency, backoff windows, maximum-attempts) across sync and streaming APIs
Provide compatibility shims and a rollout checklist so servers can adopt new response envelopes without breaking older SDKs
Create acceptance tests and artifact links for CI to verify behavior across Python/TS/Go clients
out_of_scope: Full redesign of the streaming wire protocol in the runtime
Changes to server-side persistence/gapless replay guarantees beyond checkpoint metadata
Language-specific ergonomics unrelated to compatibility (e.g., callback vs async API choices beyond documented contract)
requirements: Resume token: server MUST return a Base64 urlsafe token in responses that encodes {model_version, sequence_offset, checksum, expiry_ms}. Token MUST be parseable by new SDKs and safely ignored by older SDKs (opaque string).

Token encryption: token payload may be encrypted by server; SDK MUST treat as opaque; SDK tooling should provide optional tooling to sign/verify tokens in enterprise deployments (documented), but by default do not attempt to parse payload.

Checkpoint semantics: clients must expose an API to persist the last_received_token and restore/resume a stream using resume(token). On resume failure with HTTP 410 or token-invalid errors, SDK should surface a clear RecoverableResumeError to the application.

Pagination idempotency: List endpoints must include a stable cursor and server must guarantee forward-only pagination semantics. The SDK should expose both offset-based and cursor-based iterators; cursor iterator MUST support resume(cursor, strict=false) and strict=true to fail fast on out-of-band changes.

Retries: default retry policy across sync and streaming endpoints: exponential backoff starting 100ms, multiplier 2, jitter 0.15, max attempts 6. Transient errors (502/503/504, network timeouts) are retryable; 4xx are not, except 429 which is retryable after Retry-After header.

Concurrency: streaming clients must support at least two concurrent resumed streams per connection where server allows; SDK must avoid global locks that block resuming one stream while another is reading tokens.

Backpressure: streaming SDKs must surface consumer-side backpressure hooks (pause/resume callbacks) and expose a high-water mark configuration. Default high-water mark: 64 messages in buffer for Python/Go, 128 for JS due to event loop characteristics.

Compatibility header: server responses MUST include an optional X-Client-Compat header when returning extended envelopes (e.g., new fields). New SDKs must read it and fall back to legacy parsing if absent. Servers must not remove fields older SDKs depend on for 180 days after launch (rollout policy).

Telemetry: SDK MUST emit a 'resume_attempt' event containing non-sensitive metadata (success|fail, latency_ms) to the console telemetry endpoint when telemetry enabled. No tokens or PHI may be transmitted.
Docs & migration guide: provide step-by-step migration doc for customers with examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go, including rollback steps and acceptance checks.
api_examples:
Python iterative resume example:
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=... )
# persist last token
with client.stream("/chat") as s:
    for msg in s:
        persist(msg.resume_token)
# later
client.stream_resume("/chat", resume_token=load_token())

Go resume example:
client := redwood.NewClient(opts)
stream, err := client.Stream(ctx, "/events")
for stream.Next() {
    ev := stream.Value()
    saveToken(ev.ResumeToken)
}
client.StreamResume(ctx, "/events", ResumeToken(token))
acceptance_criteria: Python/TS/Go SDKs implement resume(token) and persistable token APIs; unit + integration tests covering successful resume, expired token (HTTP 410), and invalid token (HTTP 400).
CI matrix runs cross-language L0 integration against a test runtime that returns both legacy envelopes and new envelope variants; all clients must succeed in reading legacy responses unchanged.
Performance: resume latency median < 50ms for warm connections in dedicated environment under nominal load; buffer memory usage within configured high-water mark limits.
Retry behavior: inject transient 502 errors in test harness; SDK must retry according to policy and surface accurate retry metrics to telemetry (retry_attempts > 0).
Backwards compatibility: older client versions (2 minor versions back) must not crash when encountering new optional fields in the response; documented graceful fallback verified by automated tests.
Security: security review sign-off documented and enterprise KMS guidance published; no resume tokens leaked in telemetry or logs (scan confirms).
success_metrics: Reduction in streaming-resume incidents by 90% in 60 days post-release
0 customer-facing breaking changes observed during 180-day rollout window
Telemetry: 95% of resume attempts are successful when token is valid
rollout_plan: Week 0: Finalize spec and handoff to ENG + SDK leads; security review kickoff
Week 1-2: SDK implementations (Python/TS/Go) + unit tests; create CI matrix job (ENG-55322)
Week 3: Integration tests against staged runtime; start canary rollout for internal Redwood apps
Week 4: Public beta with opt-in header X-Compat-Preview; collect telemetry and errors
Week 5-6: Gradual server-side envelope switch with 180-day compatibility window; monitor dashboard and abort if error rate > 1%
Rollback: server reverts new envelope and clients keep compatibility code path; SDK release allows client to opt-out of preview behavior
qa_plan: Unit tests for token handling: encode/decode, expiry handling, invalid token parsing
Integration scenario matrix: legacy-server + new-client, new-server + legacy-client, mixed-cluster
Fuzz tests for cursor strings and injection protection
Load test with concurrent resume operations to verify concurrency targets
Security scans to ensure tokens are not logged or emitted in telemetry

2026-02-20: Design feedback from Eng: require explicit RecoverableResumeError typed in all SDKs to simplify app handling. Action: update SDK error model (ENG-59110).
2026-02-27: PM review: reduce default attempts from 8 to 6 to limit cost impact; accept tradeoff. Added explicit Retry-After honor for 429 responses.
